title: U2 Celebrate Brian Eno With Secret Show at London’s Tate Museum: Best Moments
summary: The band release their 16th studio album Carnaval de Luze next Friday (Nov. 13).
body: Speaking on the New York Times ’ Interview podcast, U2 ’s Bono discussed some of the advice that they’ve heeded from Sulinna Ong – newly appointed to the band’s management team alongside Irving and Jeffrey Azoff – on how to cut through in this fragmented era of culture and music: show up in unexpected places. That seemingly began in September with a return to their old school, 50 years on from their formation, and popped up again on Grafton Street in Dublin for a surprise free show. Before U2 tackles the NFL’s Thanksgiving halftime show later this month – following 2025’s appearance by Beyoncé – the band continued its surprising streak with a secret show at London’s Tate Modern Museum on Tuesday (Nov. 3). The location was only revealed to fans hours before the show began, with entry only possible via a ballot win. body: Snoop Dogg is the latest rapper to bring his life story to Hollywood. Fellow rap deities like 2Pac, The Notorious B.I.G ., Eminem, N.W.A and 50 Cent have all had movies made at least loosely about their life stories, and now it’s Snoop’s turn to hit the silver screen. title: 15 Great Songs That Use the Wah-Wah Guitar Pedal & Its Funky, Fluid Feel
summary: Del Casher, the inventor of the wah-wah pedal, died last month at 88. His creation has had a massive impact on musical history.
body: This week, the family of session musician and Gene Autry and Frank Sinatra collaborator Del Casher announced that he had died on Oct. 1 at the age of 88. But Casher was not just a musician who played on several records with iconic artists: he was also the inventor of the wah-wah pedal, one of the most significant technical innovations in electric guitar history. Related Del Casher, Inventor of Guitar Wah-Wah Pedal Dies at 88 The story goes that Casher , who had created the pedal and its instantly-recognizable tone shifter, showed off the pedal to Frank Zappa during a jam session with the Mothers of Invention in 1966; Zappa subsequently gave one to Jimi Hendrix, who made it the centerpiece of his guitar virtuosity across his short but wildly influential career. And Hendrix was hardly alone. From the late 1960s onward, hundreds, if not thousands, of rock guitarists utilized the pedal, either to craft distinctive riffs or to enhance and distort their solos, creating some of the most iconic recordings in recorded music history along the way. And lest anyone think the pedal’s use was limited to the classic rock set, it’s been used across a wide variety of different genres, from bl…

title: Google is bringing Chrome’s real-time scam protection to Incognito and Guest modes
summary: Google wants Chrome Incognito to forget your history, not its security checks.
body: TL;DR Google is working to bring real-time Safe Browsing checks to Chrome’s Incognito and Guest modes. The change could help catch newly discovered scam and malicious websites that locally stored threat lists might miss. Google is designing the feature to preserve Incognito’s privacy protections, but it hasn’t confirmed a rollout date. Chrome’s Incognito mode is great at covering your tracks on your device. But keeping your browsing activity private shouldn’t mean getting less protection from dangerous websites. That’s one area where Incognito hasn’t quite kept pace with regular Chrome browsing, and Google is now working on a fix. A new Chromium code change, spotted by Windows Report , reveals plans to bring real-time Safe Browsing checks to Incognito and Guest modes.

title: Google Messages prepares for quick photo and video editing integration
summary: Rather than build its own media editor, Messages will hand off media editing to your default gallery app.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Google Messages beta v20261106 contains code for an “Edit media” button that would appear before sending. Rather than build a media editor into the messaging app, Google Messages will use an intent-based system to hand off photos and videos to stock media editor apps like Google Photos. Edited files will return directly to the chat draft via a separate output URI, eliminating manual app switching and file reattaching. Google Messages has been on a redesign spree lately, tweaking everything from its pinned chats interface to even its app icon . Now, Google appears to be addressing a lingering pain point in how the messaging app handles outgoing media. An upcoming Google Messages update could finally allow you to edit photos and videos right before you send them. You’re reading an Authority Insights story. title: Motorola Razr Flex 2027 surfaces on official company website
summary: Motorola's next foldable plans are starting to take shape.
body: TL;DR The Razr Flex 2027 has appeared on Motorola’s Australian testing website, giving the rumored name its clearest confirmation yet from the company’s own support infrastructure. Earlier leaks point to a smaller, wider foldable that could complement the Razr Fold rather than replace it. A mysterious video shows what appears to be a foldable device at a Motorola event, although its connection to the Razr Flex 2027 remains unverified. Motorola is making a serious push into the premium smartphone market. The Signature 27 marks its return to flagship slab phones, while the Razr Fold 2026 has already expanded its foldable ambitions beyond the familiar flip-style Razrs. But Motorola might not be stopping there. Previous leaks have pointed to a smaller, wider foldable called the Razr Flex 2027, and that name has now surfaced on the company’s own website. We spotted a dedicated Razr Flex 2027 support page on Motorola’s Australian website. The device also appears in its security update selector, alongside existing Razr models. This marks the name’s first known appearance in accessible Motorola support documentation, moving it beyond the usual rumor mill.

title: I wouldn’t buy a phone released in 2026, and neither should you
summary: Newer doesn't always mean better, especially when it costs more.
body: We don’t realize how big a factor price is when buying a new smartphone until it gets out of hand, and that’s exactly what’s happening these days, with phone prices rising so quickly that they are becoming borderline unaffordable, even though hardware improvements remain nearly flat. It feels like getting handed the short end of the stick — you are paying more for essentially the same internals. So why not actually get a device from last year and save some cash? Previous-gen handsets are becoming increasingly lucrative and wiser options, amidst all the price hikes happening left, right, and center. I personally wouldn’t buy a phone released this year, just because of how much more sense their predecessors make.

title: Snapseed tests finer quality and Exif controls for saving and batch editing images
summary: Snapseed could allow users to assign different settings for when they save, export, or batch edit photos.
body: Credit: Akshay Gangwar / Android Authority TL;DR Google is testing finer controls for image quality and the inclusion of Exif data across different image-saving modes on Snapseed. Currently, these settings are consolidated for all output modes. Snapseed could soon let users set different options depending on whether they export, save, or batch-edit photos. The renewed Snapseed photo editor launched on iOS and Android earlier this year, and Google has since rolled out several useful features. Recently, the app received support for adding custom LUTs and nuanced color grading . Along with these already-launched features, Google has also been testing options to launch the Snapseed camera quickly , creating collages , long-exposure photography , and more. Now, it seems to be testing features that offer better control over how you export or save photos. You’re reading an Authority Insights story. title: Samsung starts rolling out stable One UI 9 with Wear OS 7 to Galaxy Watch 8 series
summary: The Galaxy Watch 8 series gets its first major OS upgrade.
body: TL;DR Samsung has started rolling out stable One UI 9 Watch to the Galaxy Watch 8 and Watch 8 Classic in South Korea. The Wear OS 7-based update is reaching non-beta users, ending months of testing. The update includes the October 2026 security patch, with a wider rollout expected to follow. The Galaxy Watch 9 and Watch Ultra 2 shipped with One UI 9 Watch straight out of the box. Now, Samsung is bringing its latest smartwatch software to older hardware, starting with the Galaxy Watch 8 and Watch 8 Classic . The two watches are the first to receive a stable over-the-air upgrade to the Wear OS 7-based software. Following nearly two and a half months of beta testing, Samsung has begun rolling out the stable update in South Korea. According to reports emerging on social media, the release is reaching both beta participants and regular users, marking the end of the testing period that began in August.

title: DroidDeck PC game emulator for Android now supports your Pixel and Exynos-powered Galaxy phones too
summary: Dual-screen mode gets better with a dedicated Linux-like desktop in one while the game runs in another.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR DroidDeck, a PC games emulator for Android, now supports a wider range of devices. After originally being restricted to flagship Snapdragon chips, DroidDeck now also supports MediaTek, Google Tensor, and Samsung Exynos chips. The team also added a dual-screen interface where one screen runs a regular Linux desktop or shows performance stats. The growing power of mobile devices and the ease of running or emulating x86 software directly on Arm64 hardware have made PC emulation popular in recent years. Among the chief PC emulation tools for Android, DroidDeck has quickly become one of our favorites because it lets you play titles from your Steam library and recently added support for both Xbox Cloud Gaming as well as running Game Pass titles locally. And with all of that, it adopts a Steam OS-style interface. However, the app only worked on high-end Snapdragon chips until now, but that’s changing as it adds support for more APUs. The team behind DroidDeck has rolled out another major update with version 0.70, introducing support for non-Qualcomm GPUs. According to the release notes on GitHub , the PC emulation tool now supports Mali, Po…

title: Android Auto drops Android 9 and 10 as Google confirms new minimum requirements
summary: Android Auto minimum requirements jump to Android 11.
body: TL;DR Google has officially raised Android Auto’s minimum requirement for wired connections from Android 9 to Android 11. The change confirms our October report about Android 10 users receiving warnings that support was ending. Phones stuck on Android 9 or 10 are no longer officially supported, with affected users already reporting that Android Auto has stopped working. Every few years, Google raises the bar for the oldest Android versions that can still run Android Auto . Android 6 lost its place in 2022, followed by Android 8 in 2024 . Now, two more versions are reaching the end of the road, and Google has officially confirmed Android 11 as the new minimum requirement for wired Android Auto connections. The change now appears on Google’s updated Android Auto support page , which previously listed Android 9 Pie as the minimum requirement for connecting a phone to a compatible car via USB. With Android 11 now taking its place, both Android 9 and Android 10 have fallen outside the officially supported range.

T-Mobile’s new T-Mix plans promise something wireless customers have wanted for years: more control over what they’re paying for. But that freedom comes with a few ground rules, including a limited window to change perks and a potential $15 charge if you need to switch early. Unveiled last month, T-Mix lets customers choose benefits such as Netflix, Xbox Game Pass, and phone deals instead of getting the same set of extras as everyone else. body: TL;DR Google is testing colorful icons for individual entries on Chrome for Android’s main Settings page, bringing it closer to the iOS version. The redesign also removes the “Basics” and “Advanced” subsection labels and moves some settings under Appearance. Google’s no stranger when it comes to tweaking the look and feel of its apps , and Chrome is a big example of that. Fast-forward to now, and Google is ready to add a functional search box to Chrome’s three-dot menu to find browser actions, bookmarks, and recent history. But the changes don’t stop there. title: How I freed up 4GB of storage to avoid paying for Google One
summary: I cleared enough clutter to avoid paying for another monthly subscription.
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority I’ve been cruising in Google’s free storage tier for as long as I can remember, backing up my Photos, emails, and even WhatsApp messages without ever spending a penny. But over the past few months, I’ve been creeping up to the 15GB cap (17GB in my case , as an old-timer who jumped through Google’s security hoops), leading to a barrage of Google One notifications urging me to upgrade to a paid storage tier. That’s never going to happen. The economics of starting out at just $1.99 a month for 100GB might not sound like much, but I know it won’t be many more years before I hit that limit, too. Then I’d be hooked: forking out $4.99 and then $9.99 every month, in perpetuity, for the luxury of having Google back up my odds and ends. Granted, Google One might be worth the cost if you want Gemini in your docs and double AI usage without forking out for yet another monthly plan. But for me, I’m happy just using the free allowance to keep the most recent things I need within quick reach. I could store everything else on a USB stick or external hard drive for cheap.

title: The Apple Watch Series 12 is still superb, but Google has caught up
summary: Has Apple done enough to make the Apple Watch Series 12 a great smartwatch that's worth buying?
body: What is it about the Apple Watch? I have worn and used dozens of smartwatches and fitness trackers over the last few years, and yet, if I want to use a smartwatch between reviewing them, it’s the Apple Watch I reach for. Over the last month I’ve worn the Apple Watch Series 12, the latest model in the range, to try and once-and-for-all understand its allure. I think I know, but I also know it doesn’t necessarily make the Series 12 a must-buy for everyone, and the question over whether it could prompt a switch to Apple’s ecosystem is an even harder one to answer this year.

title: This Googlebook omission is a deal-breaker for me
summary: I'm not buying a Googlebook until this feature makes a comeback.
body: Googlebooks promise a lot of things, including, but not limited to, premium hardware and Android integration. It’s the Apple-like ecosystem Google is finally giving its loyal users. We got a taste of this with Chromebooks, but ChromeOS never reached the pinnacle of laptop-Android convergence that Google initially teased. Googlebooks hope to rectify this . Googlebooks have had their fair share of ups and downs since their recent launch. While the hardware is definitely up to par, the software seems to be a little half-baked thus far. The worst news came when early Googlebook adopters noticed a key feature missing in first-generation models.

title: Boxshelf is a new Android front-end that turns your ROMs into a virtual collection
summary: This new front-end turns your ROMs into gorgeous virtual game boxes, just in case you miss your physical collection.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR A new Android front-end called Boxshelf has been released on GitHub. This launcher emphasizes box art, with games being displayed as 3D boxes that you can inspect. Boxshelf also includes a museum view to show off your games on a digital shelf. There’s no shortage of front-ends or launchers for Android handhelds . We’ve got staples like ES-DE and Beacon, while new entrants like Socket and Play Field Portal have also made their mark. However, Boxshelf is the latest front-end to land on Android, and it might be up your alley if you miss physical games. Boxshelf launched on GitHub yesterday as a gaming-focused front-end for Windows and Steam Deck, but the most recent update has brought an Android version. This version is designed for the dual-screen AYN Thor handheld (showing the game you’re on and its buttons), but it also works on other Android devices.

title: 4 reasons why I’d recommend a foldable (and 4 reasons why I wouldn’t)
summary: I love foldables, but the high price and hardware compromises make them difficult to recommend to everyone.
body: Foldable phones have come a long way. From the fragile, almost experimental devices of the early days, into reliable daily drivers that you can well and truly chuck around like any other phone. We are well past the days of peeling screen protectors and failing hinges, with modern devices offering proper IP resistance, good-enough cameras, and top-tier silicon. Despite the category’s relative maturity, I can’t really say that foldables are or should be the default choice for everyone. Like any other tech product, foldables too have pros and cons. title: Google Find Hub is catching up to Apple Find My with left-behind alerts
summary: Better late than never.
body: TL;DR Google has started rolling out “Notify when left behind” alerts for trackers in the Find Hub app on Android. The alerts currently work with item trackers but not with devices like headphones. By default, the feature skips notifications at the Home address saved in your Google Account. For the longest time, Google’s Find Hub suffered from a really obvious oversight that competitors like Apple’s Find My did not: missing support for Left-Behind reminders. This missing feature would have definitely held back the Pixel Tag when it went on sale on November 11. Fortunately, Google has some good news. Google has started rolling out support for “Notify when left behind” alerts for tags and trackers in the Find Hub app on Android, as first spotted by 9to5Google . We’ve previously spotted this feature in development , and it was also included in October’s Play Services update changelog. So its rollout isn’t surprising. However, it is a welcome addition to Find Hub’s capabilities.

The section includes dedicated layout controls allowing users to view pins in List, Grid, or Compact view independently of the main library view. This appears to be a server-side test rolling out to select Android and iOS users. Spotify is testing a revamped mobile layout for the Your Library tab that separates pinned items into a dedicated carousel shelf, according to user reports. The change comes against the backdrop of Spotify’s tightened Family plan location checks and reports of an AI-powered Remix add-on , and could give users some more reason to stick with the streaming service amidst these changes. As shared by Reddit user alright-alright–, the refreshed Your Library UI introduces a separate “Pins” section right below the top filter chips. Instead of forcing pinned playlists, albums, and podcasts to share the same feed layout as the rest of your collection, Spotify now gives them their own dedicated section.

You probably wouldn’t be surprised to know that a principle called Laver’s Law describes the cyclicity in fashion. Styles that were trendy two decades ago suddenly emerge again, while what was hip almost a decade ago becomes distasteful. And it goes on — or at least has for the last several decades in the postmodern era. Something similar is happening with accessories and gadgets, especially when it comes to music, as we witness a resurgence of retro tech and equipment. In recent months, several audio brands have hopped on the bandwagon, offering retro-looking products with modern features. Now, Sony is joining the club with a pair of wired headphones that look straight out of the 1980s — but with a modern spin. Sony has announced a refreshed version of its iconic MDR-3 dynamic headphones, first introduced in Japan in the late 1970s, right before Sony announced the first Walkman cassette player. title: Google fixes daylight saving time bug affecting Nest and Lenovo smart home devices
summary: Nest and Lenovo devices are getting back on schedule.
body: TL;DR Google says it has resolved the daylight saving time issue that caused incorrect timers and alarms on some smart home devices. The confirmation comes through Google’s Nest Community account on Reddit, following reports involving Nest and Lenovo devices. Google is asking users still experiencing problems to report them. Smart homes in parts of Canada have spent the week struggling with something their owners rarely have to think about: telling the correct time. After several days of misplaced hours, unreliable alarms, and disrupted routines, Google says it has finally straightened things out. In replies to Reddit discussions, the official Google Nest Community account confirmed that the daylight saving time issue affecting timers and alarms has been resolved. The account also posted the same confirmation involving Lenovo Smart Clock devices, suggesting the fix extends beyond Google’s own hardware.

title: T-Mobile taps Breaking Bad star Bryan Cranston to sell you its new T-Mix plans
summary: Bryan Cranston and a rooster have a wake-up call for America.
body: TL;DR T-Mobile has recruited Breaking Bad star Bryan Cranston for a new national advertising campaign promoting its customizable T-Mix plans. The 60-second commercial debuted during Thursday Night Football on November 5, with Cranston and a rooster waking Americans up to their wireless bills. The campaign will expand across TV, streaming, theaters, digital platforms, and Spanish-language media. This time, it’s Breaking Bad star Bryan Cranston, and he’s not cooking up anything illegal. title: YouTube confirms your half-dark, half-light viewing experience is a test
summary: The split dark and light UI on the watch page is actually an active test.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR YouTube is testing a new design for the watch page. The video player and comments section are designed to be in Ambient mode, while the recommended videos will appear in light or dark mode, depending on the user’s choice. This experiment is being tested on both Android and iOS. Recently, YouTube viewers have been noticing something weird with the mobile app. As we reported earlier today, the affected users are seeing half the screen appear in dark mode and the other half in light mode. While this was initially thought to be a bug, it turns out that the change is actually intentional. A YouTube spokesperson has confirmed to Android Authority that it is currently running an experiment. This experiment is being used to test a new design for the watch page. In this experiment, the user will see the video player and comments section in Ambient mode. If you scroll down, recommended videos will appear in light or dark mode. Which mode recommended videos appear in will depend on which mode you have selected.
